Brastias.json.text: Brastias was an Arthurian knight. He served Gorlois, the duke of Cornwall. He helped the disguised Uther Pendragon reach the chamber of Igraine, the duke's wife. The magician Merlin had changed Uther's face so he looked like Gorlois home from battle. This knight welcomed Uther inside on Merlin's behalf. Arthur was conceived with Igraine that same night. After Arthur became king, Brastias ranked among his most loyal nobles.

Bres.json.text: Bres is an Irish god. Several figures share this name. The chief one was Bres mac Elatha. He was originally called Eochu. His beauty earned him the nickname Bres, meaning the beautiful one. His mother was the Tuatha Dé Danann princess Ériu or Eithne. His father was the Fomorian king Elatha. As king of Tara he held back fire and gave guests only plain crackers. He even denied drink to a bard. Cairbre mac Éadoine answered with a sharp satire. Boils broke out on Bres's face. A blemished king could not rule. The people drove him from the throne. He joined his father's forces and lost the second battle of Mag Tuired. In some accounts his consort was the goddess Brigit. Their son Ruadán died at Mag Tuired. Another Bres fell in the first battle of Mag Tuired. A Bres also rules Hy-Brâzil, an island of the Otherworld.

Brian.json.text: Brian is an Irish god. The popular Irish name comes from him. He belonged to the Tuatha Dé Danann and was one of the tragic Sons of Tuireann. His mother was the goddess Danu. His father was the hero Tuireann. Brian and his two brothers ambushed Cian, the father of Lugh. Cian changed into a pig, but the brothers killed him. Lugh made them complete eight impossible feats. They finished seven and failed the last, so Lugh slew them. The name also belongs to the high king Brian Boru. He rose from a tiny kingdom to rule all Ireland. He died at Clontarf while gathering forces against the Vikings.

Briccriu.json.text: Briccriu is an Irish hero. He was the bitter-tongued poet of the Ulster Cycle. He appears most in Briccriu's Feast. He pitted great champions against one another for the Champion's Portion. That rivalry caused much bloodshed. He acted the same way in the story of Mac Dathó's Pig. He died beside Loughbrickland, the lake that carries his name in Ulster. There he mocked the appetite of queen Medb. Her lover Fergus mac Róich brained him.

Brigantia.json.text: Brigantia is a goddess of the continental peoples and Britain. The northern part of the island held the Brigantes, a Brythonic folk, in early historical days. They venerated her as an ancestral deity. Her name lives on in the rivers Braint in Anglesey and Brent in Middlesex. Roman-era images and inscriptions join her with Victoria and Caelestis, the Syrian sky goddess. Her title translates as the high one. Some link her to the Irish Brigit. Scholars also tie her to the Gaulish goddess Brigindo.
